newsitem.title: Japan: Dlr stalls by Tokyo noon after hitting new high.
newsitem.headline: Dlr stalls by Tokyo noon after hitting new high.

text.p: The dollar was stuck at just above 127 yen in late morning Tokyo on Thursday after earlier rising as high as 127.18 yen, its highest since August 1992.

Lingering dollar sales to protect options positions, which will expire in New York later on in the day, kept the dollar from reaching 127.20 yen and above where a huge amount of stop-loss dollar buying was expected, dealers said.
Persistent dollar sales to avoid hitting the knock-out point of 127.30 yen, coupled with sporadic sales by Japanese exporters, put a lid on the dollar's rise, dealers said.
These options would give holders the right to buy dollars at 124 yen or 125 yen, well below current levels, unless the dollar were to touch the knock-out price of 127.30 yen before the expiry.

Opinions were divided over the dollar's direction after the expiry of these options. "I think simply that the dollar will be given leeway to advance against the yen after the expiry," said one options dealer at a U.S. bank in Tokyo.

But a Japanese bank dealer said profit-taking may emerge from options holders who were able to buy dollars cheaply. There would be different kinds of option positions which could induce profit-taking above 127.30 yen, dealers said.

"In addition, there is also wariness over possible BOJ (Bank of Japan) intervention on rises after stop-loss buying at 127.30 yen," said the Japanese bank dealer. Exporters have also started arranging long-term forward dollar sales, he added.
Meanwhile, the dollar's downside was firmly supported by upbeat U.S. economic data on Wednesday, which reignited speculation of higher U.S. interest rates, dealers said.

Overnight, the dollar rallied to session highs after the Commerce Department reported the economy grew 5.6 percent during the first three months of this year -- its fastest clip in more than nine years. It also prompted celebration in U.S. stock and bond markets with the Dow Jones industrials rising above 7,000 level for the first time since March 13.

There was talk overnight that the Bank of France might have sold dollars against the mark at 1.7330-35 marks, making the dollar's topside heavy at above 1.7350 marks in Tokyo, said the Japanese bank dealer.
